solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Singer of 'Don't Dilly Dally …' mistakenly Dolly

indicators.note: something done mistakenly comes out wrong, so the letters are set down in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone misattributes the old music-hall number to a singer called Dolly.
explanation.walkthrough: Marie Lloyd was a British music-hall star whose famous song begins 'My old man said follow the van, and don't dilly dally on the way'.
explanation.definitionFit: Marie Lloyd is the music-hall performer who made that song famous, so her surname identifies the singer.

clue.text: Miss going round Balearic capital and port

indicators.note: one thing going round another encloses it, so the first word's letters wrap the second

parts.note: a miss is a girl or young woman, a lass
Palma is the capital of Majorca and the Balearic Islands

explanation.surface: A young woman travels around the main city of the Balearics and its harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Balearic capital' wants to sit in the answer as a place, and it does, but only as the inner piece; the port itself is in the Canaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Las Palmas, on Gran Canaria, is a major Spanish seaport.

clue.text: Where seeds might be having continued success

definitions.meaning: first meaning: sesame or poppy seeds sit on top of a bread bun
second meaning: enjoying a winning streak

explanation.surface: Top seeds in a tournament keep winning their matches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seeds' suggests tennis players, which suits the success half; the other half is the baker's bun with seeds on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on a roll is an idiom for a run of good luck, and seeds are literally scattered on a bread roll.

clue.text: Scolding wild dog with raised tail

indicators.note: in a down entry raising the tail lifts the final letter higher up the word, rearranging it

parts.note: the dingo is the Australian wild dog

explanation.surface: Someone tells off a wild dog that holds its tail up.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one letter moves: the last letter of DINGO climbs to second place to give DOING. A 'doing' is British slang for a telling-off or beating.
explanation.definitionFit: In British informal speech a doing is a severe reprimand, a synonym for a scolding.

clue.text: Tire employees that could support Blue Peter perhaps

definitions.text: that could support Blue Peter perhaps

parts.note: to flag is to tire or weaken
a firm's employees are its staff

explanation.surface: Tired workers who might help out on a children's television programme.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue Peter is a long-running BBC children's TV show, but it is named after a real flag, the blue-and-white one hoisted when a ship is about to sail.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagstaff is the pole that holds up a flag, and the Blue Peter is a nautical signal flag.

clue.text: Dutch provincial is returning article after one day

parts.note: Fri is the short form of Friday, one day of the week

indicators.note: something returning heads back the way it came, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written, then turned round
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A person from a Dutch province comes back with a news piece a day later.
explanation.definitionFit: Friesland is a province of the Netherlands, and a native of it is a Frisian.

clue.text: Mild disease isn't commonly restricting climber at intervals

indicators.note: restricting something hems it in, so one set of letters closes around the other

parts.note: ain't is the common, colloquial form of isn't

indicators.note: taking letters at intervals means picking every other one and skipping the rest

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of climber

explanation.surface: A minor illness that, contrary to rumour, doesn't hold back a mountaineer now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: An ailment is a minor illness or complaint, a disorder that is not serious.

clue.text: Peter clear of all charges including totally voided insurance, for one

indicators.note: including something means taking it inside, so the short piece goes within the longer phrase

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe

indicators.note: a word that is voided has its insides emptied, so only its two end letters survive

parts.note: the first and last letters of totally
a net sum is what is left after all deductions

explanation.surface: A man named Peter is acquitted of every charge, an outcome his insurance had totally failed to cover.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter looks like a man's name; in old crooks' slang a peter is a safe, as in a safe-breaker being a peterman.
explanation.definitionFit: Insurance is one example of a safety net, a protection against loss or failure.

clue.text: Lover for the most part sullen amongst teetotallers

indicators.note: being amongst others means sitting between them, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: AA, Alcoholics Anonymous, is a body of teetotallers

indicators.note: for the most part means most but not all, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: morose means sullen and gloomy

explanation.surface: A sweetheart who is mostly glum when surrounded by non-drinkers.
explanation.walkthrough: AA, Alcoholics Anonymous, is the crossword's stock source for teetotallers.
explanation.definitionFit: Amorosa is an Italian-derived word for a female lover or sweetheart.

clue.text: Starts to feel uncomfortable, turning over new mattress

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so only the initial of each word is kept

parts.note: the initials of the five words

explanation.surface: Someone begins to feel uncomfortable and keeps rolling over on a new bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads naturally as restless sleep; the instructions just take the first letter of each of the following words.
explanation.definitionFit: A futon is a thin padded mattress, Japanese in origin, often laid on a floor or frame.

clue.text: People from Israel by a hotel in Kensington?

indicators.note: being in a place means being within it, so these letters are placed inside the postcode

parts.note: SW1 is a central London postcode, with the 1 written as I; the question mark admits Kensington is not quite in it
taken as written
Hotel is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for H
IL is Israel's international country code

explanation.surface: Israelis staying beside a hotel in a smart part of west London.
explanation.walkthrough: Kensington is a wealthy district of London with SW postcodes; the clue treats it as SW1, with the digit 1 standing for I. 'People from Israel' looks like the definition but only 'People' is.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swahili are a Bantu people of the East African coast and Zanzibar, who give their name to the language.

clue.text: Excluded potential slogan of present-day Tories

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a rallying cry to get the political ... of office

explanation.walkthrough: The Tories are Britain's Conservative Party, now in opposition to a Labour government; 'Left out!' is what they might chant, and also what they are.
explanation.definitionFit: Left out is an ordinary phrase for omitted or excluded, and as a slogan it demands removal of the left-wing government.

clue.text: Close to dealing with half of so-so cast

indicators.note: taking half of a doubled word keeps one of its two identical parts and drops the other
something cast is thrown or moulded afresh, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
one of the two halves of so-so

explanation.surface: Nearly coping with a cast of only middling actors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dealing with' reads as one phrase meaning handling, but dealing is fodder and with only joins it to the other piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Alongside means beside or next to, the same as close to something.

clue.text: Old English character, prickly thing, author naively pens

indicators.note: a phrase that pens something encloses it, so the letters lie within the run of words

parts.note: letters running across the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A writer innocently includes an ancient letter and a sharp spike.
explanation.walkthrough: Unusually there are two definitions as well as the wordplay: the old runic letter and the spine on a stem.
explanation.definitionFit: Thorn was a letter of the Old English alphabet, written þ, and a thorn is also a sharp spike on a plant.

clue.text: Huge amount of money in box number one withdrawn

parts.note: to mill is old slang for to fight with fists, to box

indicators.note: withdrawn means pulled back, so the letters are read in the backward direction

parts.note: NO for number and I for one, then turned round

explanation.surface: Someone takes a fortune out of a numbered strongbox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' looks like a container for the money; here it is the verb to fight, and a mill is an old word for a boxing match.
explanation.definitionFit: A million, short for a million pounds or dollars, stands for a vast sum of money.

clue.text: Faint line scrawled around half of clock face in gold and black

indicators.note: letters placed around others enclose them
one piece placed in others sits inside them
a scrawled word is written messily, so its letters come out jumbled
half of a word keeps only some of its letters and drops the rest

parts.note: taken as written, then jumbled
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a clock's face is its dial; only the first half is used
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A faint line drawn round half a clock face picked out in gold and black.
explanation.walkthrough: Line looks like part of the picture being drawn, but it is the jumbled outer shell; 'faint' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A faint sound may be inaudible, too quiet to be heard.

clue.text: Vessel's capacity to date includes a couple of unspecified numbers

indicators.note: a phrase that includes something holds it inside itself

parts.note: taken as written
N stands for an unspecified number, as in the nth degree; two of them
to date is to grow old or show one's age

explanation.surface: A ship's carrying capacity so far includes a pair of unknown figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To date' reads as one phrase meaning so far; here it splits, and date is the verb meaning grow old.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonnage is the carrying capacity of a ship, measured in tons.

clue.text: Film's legal clause presenting few difficulties initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, telling you which of the two pieces goes first in the answer

parts.note: something that presents few difficulties is easy
a rider is a clause added to a legal document

explanation.surface: A movie's contract clause turns out to be straightforward at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' tells you the easy piece comes first in the answer, though it comes second in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy Rider is the 1969 road movie starring Peter Fonda and Dennis Hopper.

clue.text: Charge to keep military men in field of action

indicators.note: a place that keeps something holds it within, so the outer word wraps the inner one

parts.note: a stage is the arena where events take place
OR is the abbreviation for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A fee for housing soldiers in a battle zone.
explanation.walkthrough: Charge looks like a military attack, which fits the soldiers; it is the fee paid for keeping goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Storage is the fee paid for having goods kept in a warehouse, so it names a charge.

clue.text: Tragic hero's extremely over-confident greeting

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so just the first and last letters are taken

parts.note: the first and last letters of over-confident
a common greeting

explanation.surface: A doomed protagonist says hi a little too confidently.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello is the title hero of Shakespeare's tragedy, the Moor who kills Desdemona.

clue.text: Ban bad-tempered sort upset about business qualification

indicators.note: letters placed about something surround it
in a down entry something upset is turned upside down, so its letters run the other way

parts.note: an ogre is a monstrous, ill-tempered person
MBA is the Master of Business Administration degree

explanation.surface: A grumpy type, upset over a business degree, bars something.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official prohibition, especially on trade, so it is a ban.

clue.text: Dire Straits, musical performers

indicators.note: something dire is in a dreadful state, so the letters of the next word are in a mess

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Dire Straits, the British rock band, described as musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: The band's name reads as a single proper noun, but its first word is the instruction and its second the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Recording musicians and performers are commonly called artists in the music business.

clue.text: Fatty creamy mixture covered by Larousse off and on

indicators.note: something covered by another is wrapped inside it
off and on means intermittently, so letters are alternately skipped and kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of Larousse
a dip is a creamy sauce for dunking

explanation.surface: A rich sauce mentioned only intermittently in the Larousse cookery book.
explanation.walkthrough: Larousse is the French publisher famous for its encyclopedia of cookery, which fits the creamy picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Adipose is the technical adjective for fatty, as in adipose tissue.

clue.text: Quickly examine in detail case of leprosy with probes

indicators.note: something that probes pushes its way inside, so the short piece goes into the word

parts.note: to sift is to examine closely
W is the abbreviation for with

indicators.note: a case is the outer shell of something, so only the two outside letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of leprosy

explanation.surface: A doctor quickly runs tests on a leprosy patient using probes.
explanation.definitionFit: Swiftly is an adverb meaning rapidly, the same as quickly.

clue.text: Help to catch inane priggish little pest

indicators.note: a word that catches another holds it inside

parts.note: aid means help

indicators.note: inane literally means empty, so the word loses its insides and keeps only its ends

parts.note: the first and last letters of priggish

explanation.surface: An appeal for help in catching a silly, prim little nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: Inane is used in its root sense of empty: the word keeps only its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An aphid, such as a greenfly, is a tiny sap-sucking insect that gardeners treat as a pest.

clue.text: Remove cap from thin projectile

indicators.note: in a down entry the cap is the top, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: narrow means thin

explanation.surface: Take the cap off a slim missile.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrow is the missile shot from a bow, so it is a projectile.

clue.text: American Republican covering up fail by US naval prison officer

indicators.note: letters covering something up enclose it, so the inner piece is hidden between them

parts.note: brig is American naval slang for a ship's prison
A is a standard abbreviation for American
to die is to fail or stop working, as an engine dies
R stands for Republican

explanation.surface: A US Republican hushes up a failure at a navy jail, for the sake of a senior officer.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists the brig last, but it opens the answer because the rest comes 'by' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigadier is a senior army officer, ranking above a colonel.

clue.text: Publicity section in trouble for 30 days

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits within it

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
PR, public relations, is a firm's publicity department

explanation.surface: The PR department has been in hot water for a month.
explanation.walkthrough: '30 days' reads as a length of time; it pins down one month of thirty days.
explanation.definitionFit: April is one of the four months that have thirty days, as the rhyme says.

clue.text: Bellow about legal graduate's protection in estate, say

indicators.note: a word placed about another surrounds it

parts.note: to bellow is to roar
LLB is the Bachelor of Laws degree

explanation.surface: A law graduate shouts about security on a country estate.
explanation.walkthrough: An estate is a British estate car, a station wagon; 'estate' tempts you to think of land.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll bar is a strong bar built into a car to protect occupants if it overturns, and an estate is one kind of car.

clue.text: Field unit back in Colorado Desert base

indicators.note: base can mean debased or corrupted, so the word is reworked into a new order
the back of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the final letter of Colorado
taken as written

explanation.surface: A field unit pulls back to its base in the Colorado Desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colorado Desert' is a real place in California and reads as one name; the two words do separate jobs. 'Field' is magnetic, not a battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: The oersted is the CGS unit of magnetic field strength, named after the Danish physicist Hans Christian Ørsted.

clue.text: Healthy females mostly tackling difficult situations

indicators.note: tackling something means getting to grips with it, wrapping round it
mostly means not quite all, so the word drops its last letter

parts.note: women are females
to be in a hole is to be in a difficult situation

explanation.surface: Fit women generally take on hard challenges.
explanation.walkthrough: To be in a hole is a British idiom for being in difficulties.
explanation.definitionFit: Wholesome means conducive to good health, so it is a synonym for healthy.

clue.text: Bed wife that's left attorney

indicators.note: the wife has left, so that letter departs from the word

parts.note: an attorney is a lawyer
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A wife takes to the bed after walking out on her attorney.
explanation.walkthrough: The wife gives the W that leaves LAWYER.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed of rock or soil is a layer, a stratum, so the two words share a geological sense.
